reason: The cited evidence does not address Fe3O4 formation on Q235 steel, its barrier properties against chloride/oxygen, or corrosion suppression in NaCl environments. E1 discusses MnO formation on a different alloy under different conditions, and E2 describes protective Cr2O3/Al2O3/SiO2 layers in molten salts, not Fe3O4 in aqueous chloride. The key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: A dense, adherent Fe3O4 layer can be formed on Q235 steel by controlled pre-oxidation
Fe3O4 acts as a physical barrier to chloride and oxygen ingress
This barrier reduces electrochemical corrosion reactions
Pre-oxidation treatment parameters (oxygen partial pressure, humidity) control oxide layer quality
